newsitem.title: POLAND: INTERVIEW-Polish NFI 2 eyes non-portfolio firms.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW-Polish NFI 2 eyes non-portfolio firms.

text.p: National Investment Fund (NFI) No. 2 in Poland's mass privatisation scheme seeks to become an active player on the country's capital market by investing in firms outside its portfolio, the fund's president said.

"We intend to invest in firms outside the NFI programme. For example this year there are many interesting offers on the public market -- Bank Handlowy, (bank) Pekao SA, (oil holding) Nafta Polska and (copper firm) KGHM," Jan Bossak told Reuters.

Bossak said in an interview on Tuesday that his fund would consider taking part in the large offerings as far as its finances would allow, but that for the time being NFI 2 would focus on the privatisation and restructuring of its firms.

He said once the NFIs were listed and his fund's firms gradually secured strategic investors or were themselves listed, the fund would become less concerned with restructuring and act more like an investment fund.
Under Poland's mass privatisation programme, 15 NFIs were given control last year of stakes of over 60 percent in more than 500 medium-size companies.
Each fund, run by international consortia of managers, was given a leading, 33 percent stake in more than 30 companies and small equities in the remaining firms.

From May 12, the 26 million Poles who bought a participation unit in the scheme are entitled to exchange it for 15 shares, one in each fund, which are expected to start trade on the Warsaw bourse as early as mid-June.
Bossak said his fund could gain some of its capital for investment through loans but gave no further details.
He said NFI 2 concentrated on builders, chemical and electrical engineering firms but largely reflected the overall Polish economy.

"The structure of our portfolio corresponds more or less to the structure of the Polish economy though we have fewer firms representing the agriculture and food sector," he said, adding that the fund hoped to list three or four firms this year.

Bossak said this year's candidates for a listing were chemicals and plastics firm Zaklday Wlokien Chemicznych Stilon SA and metals and engineering firms Metalurgia SA, Fabryka Maszyn Gorniczych Famur SA, Fabryka Maszyn Glinik SA and Fabryka Butli Technicznych Milmet SA.
He said firms not reaching the bourse could receive strategic investors and that talks on Stilon were currently going on with Rhone Poulenc and a Korean investor, with offers likely soon.

Bossak said Famur was well advanced in negotiations on forming a joint venture with a Chinese strategic partner, while Milmet was seeking a partner to provide new technology and widen its product base, perhaps one from South Africa.

NFI 2 made a net profit of 4.96 million zlotys in the first quarter of 1997 after losing 48.6 million zlotys in all of 1996. At the end of this year's first quarter it had assets of 459.2 million zlotys.
